name: powrie

attributes.attribute: noisy spirit that racks old buildings and towers
loud noise warned of death or ill fortune

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The powrie, or dunter, is a noisy Scottish and British folk figure. Powries set up a racket in old buildings and towers. A swelling clamor marked approaching death or ill fortune for the hearer. The powrie is a house spirit whose noise warns of coming misfortune.

okr.objective: Describe the powrie as a noisy warning spirit.
key_results: Characterizes the powrie as a Scottish and British racket-making spirit
Links its loudest noise to approaching death or ill fortune
